newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close little changed, eye on payrolls.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close little changed, eye on payrolls.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed slightly stronger on Thursday, erasing losses seen earlier in the session, with the market largely focused on tomorrow's key U.S. jobs data, analysts said.

"We were pretty much sideways today," said Harvinder Kalirai, Candian analyst with New York-based I.D.E.A. "The tone of the market is quite good. The market is not too apprehensive going into the payrolls number."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.21 to C$105.21 to yield 7.542 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which gained 1/32 to yield 6.84 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 70 basis points from 72 basis points at Wednesday's close. Canadian

bonds opened slightly weaker this morning as investors took profits on recent spread narrowing, dealers said. Spreads narrowed sharply yesterday after the Bank of Canada cut short-term interest rates 25 basis points. Spreads between Canadian and U.S. bonds have narrowed since late last year on Canada's improving economic fundamentals.
Foreign and domestic buying because of Canada's improved fundamentals helped Canadian bonds rebound form this morning's losses, said one dealer.
"We have some more people liking the fundamentals in Canada," said the dealer, who described trading as busy.
The market is now focused the release tomorrow of U.S. non-farm payrolls data for September. Payrolls are expected to rise by 166,000.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.27 to C$100.52 to yield 6.926 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 1/32 to yield 6.59 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds narrowed to 34 basis points from 39 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.48 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.03 percent.
